title: Bannerlord Co-op on Linux
description: Step-by-step Linux guide to host a Bannerlord Co-op dedicated server (Proton, Wine or umu) and join as a client: one script per distro, firewall, service and FAQ.

strings.t-f7f3c06e723c: Short answers for common setup questions.
strings.t-283ea2aa1dc4: The server and every player need identical Co-op releases and the exact Bannerlord build, not just the same major version. Check release notes and the server’s refusal logs.
strings.t-921608513c92: For direct connect: open the server UDP port on the host firewall and forward that same UDP port on your router. CGNAT (ISP shared public IP) can still block joins — ask for a public address or use a private network. Steam Join needs lobby mode and a logged-in Steam client; it does not fix every NAT issue.
strings.t-7c8c3abacbeb: What differs on Steam Deck, Bazzite and Flatpak Steam?
strings.t-8cdcb5377f59: Steam Deck: use Desktop Mode (not officially supported). Bazzite: check for Steam first — do not install a second copy. Flatpak Steam: library and permissions live in the Flatpak sandbox. Immutable hosts: prefer existing tools, Flatpak, or a tool container over changing the base OS.
strings.t-d6be1ad51c71: Which Proton version should I choose?
strings.t-54f9e875e7b5: Use the Co-op release’s recommended Proton/GE build, or one already known to run Bannerlord. Find the real proton executable — paths vary. Stock Wine 8 failed headless SERVING here; WineHQ Wine 11.0 + Xvfb was validated. Wine 9/10 and umu are untested here. Do not break a working game install just to try the server.
strings.t-7038d13548d4: Why does the server close or crash?
strings.t-9c3a91fe3d2f: Read terminal output and dedicated-server logs first. Check exact game/Co-op builds, extraction and runtime paths. Exit code 25 points to starter_log.txt under ProgramData/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/logs. Never delete saves as a shortcut.
strings.t-60ce7da277f8: Yes. Workshop can update the client before the server, or lag because releases need TaleWorlds approval. Compare exact builds and restore a compatible pair. Restart Steam only when safe for active sessions; this guide does not change subscriptions.
strings.t-dd8e6b93c80c: Does the server need a GPU or display?
strings.t-71605b42750e: A dedicated server does not need a running Bannerlord game instance. GPU/display-free Proton operation on every VPS is still unverified. Steam lobby mode needs a logged-in Steam client; direct-IP mode is separate.
strings.t-d49b6d828caf: Save cleanly and stop only the intended server. Back up its entire CoopData directory and any separate server-data folder before changing files. Extract the update separately, retain configuration and saves, match client/game builds, then verify startup.
strings.t-abb60a76712b: How do I keep it running?
strings.t-e5ba846098be: After a successful manual start, wrap the same command in a user systemd service. Check logs with journalctl --user -u YOUR_UNIT. OpenRC/runit templates vary by distro and are unverified. Never reuse a live production unit for a test.
strings.t-c1770853cf81: Under Proton, inspect the selected prefix’s drive_c/users/steamuser/Documents/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/CoopData/DedicatedServer. Logs are under logs/ and saves under Game Saves/. Confirm the paths printed at boot; --data-dir can change them. Back up before editing.
strings.t-d915cae4f42e: Use the release changelog and manifest. The Win64 .7z is distributed on the Co-op CDN and may be absent from GitHub Assets. SteamCMD is not a substitute for this archive.
strings.t-ba74354481b0: Does disabling the watchdog help Linux stutter?
strings.t-872609587be3: Official Discord reports say it can help. Rename the client watchdog directory rather than deleting it, and keep a backup. Developer caveat: crash logs are then unavailable for support. --no-watchdog is server-only. Do not change a running game.
strings.t-42f13b13a772: Can I use the Workshop dedicated server?
strings.t-2e0973f456af: Yes: the Workshop item includes DedicatedServer. Steam keeps Workshop on the latest approved release automatically, but TaleWorlds approval can lag GitHub/CDN. The host and every player must still match. Manual Modules/Coop and Workshop Co-op must not be enabled together.
strings.t-f2b6e4497570: Which ports should direct-IP players allow?
strings.t-4f4c120eefd2: Official Discord recommends UDP 4200–4201 through host, router and cloud firewall with steam:false. Steam player-hosted invites can bypass forwarding, but dedicated-server Steam listing under Proton/Wine remains unverified here.
strings.t-c52751ba2f3e: Why is the service running but there is no UDP listener?
strings.t-116b17f95200: A new server often waits for an interactive EULA answer before binding the port. Read EULA.md and LICENSE.txt, accept only if you agree, then start the service and confirm a SERVING log line. Do not automate consent or copy another server’s acceptance file.
strings.t-4cecec659833: Is Linux or Steam Deck supported?
strings.t-eef36cbdc0c8: The official FAQ states that Linux is supported but Steam Deck is not. Deck reports vary; see issue #2162. This is a Linux setup guide.
strings.t-900bddaacdf3: What if I host and play on the same PC?
strings.t-a825692972b4: The official FAQ suggests an 8-core CPU and 16 GB RAM. Linux host-and-play can stall during character transfer (issue #2095). A separate dedicated server may help; this guide does not promise a fix.
strings.t-61097f6242ac: Where are difficulty and battle settings?
strings.t-21513f8cb5b1: Check CoopData/mod-config.json; server connection settings are in CoopData/DedicatedServer/server-config.json. Stop the intended server before editing. Lower battleSize for battle performance; back up before regenerating a config with missing options.
strings.t-3d9fda7f4129: Can Epic or manually installed clients use Steam invites?
strings.t-81e45120bdf3: Steam lobbies are Steam-to-Steam. Epic and non-Steam distributions need Direct IP with the configured UDP port, or an appropriate private network. Everyone still needs identical game and Co-op builds.
strings.t-bcff40a42336: Do client and server versions match?
strings.t-1c1eea4ef518: They must. The staging resolver downloads matching client and dedicated-server assets from one release. Compare Modules/Coop/SubModule.xml with the server release tag (RESOLVED_VERSION.txt). The script warns when they differ.
strings.t-f7062606e4c3: Can I use an AI assistant?
strings.t-07ead78d148d: An AI assistant can help explain this guide, but it may miss Bannerlord-specific details or suggest incorrect fixes. Check commands against the guide before running them.

strings.t-4a94c6ecd86f: Install from Workshop or manually — not both
strings.t-e688aebe5a7b: Official Co-op Discord setup notes (6 November 2026): Workshop item 3770450698 contains DedicatedServer/BannerlordCoopServer.exe under steamapps/workshop/content/261550/3770450698/. For a manual install, extract the matching latest client so Modules/Coop/SubModule.xml exists. Enable only Co-op for the baseline test, disable other mods and War Sails, and choose No to Safe Mode. Do not combine a manual Modules/Coop copy with the Workshop module; back up and remove the redundant manual copy when switching. Workshop updates require TaleWorlds approval and may lag the release; check versions rather than assuming parity.
strings.t-9e1c40d44a93: Launch the Linux client through Steam. For SteamAPI_Init failed, restart Steam when safe; first confirm no running server depends on it. Do not change an active game or server session during a test.
strings.t-3b4e1fb1b61e: Official Discord reports describe renaming the client bin/Win64_Shipping_Client/watchdog directory to a backup name to reduce world-map stutter on Bazzite, CachyOS and Arch. Developer caveat: disabling it removes crash logs needed for support. Only do this with explicit permission, while the game is closed, and retain the backup so it can be restored. --no-watchdog is a SERVER argument only, not a client launch option. Issue: https://github.com/Bannerlord-Coop-Team/BannerlordCoop/issues/2536.
strings.t-f19e9c25b310: Add BannerlordCoopServer.exe as a non-Steam game, select GE-Proton and put --no-watchdog in the server launch options. Alternatively use the game’s Proton prefix. For safety testing, use a separate prefix and --data-dir, not an existing live server prefix or save directory. A Steam-listed lobby under Proton/Wine is still unverified; direct IP is the reproducible fallback.
strings.t-31bbc9d9ffc0: Official Discord direct-IP instructions use steam:false in server-config.json and UDP 4200–4201 through the host firewall, router and cloud firewall. The configured main port defaults to 4200. Steam player-hosting Join Game/invites can avoid port forwarding and CGNAT; do not assume dedicated-server Steam hosting under Proton/Wine has the same verified behavior. Turn off conflicting VPN/DNS-routing tools only after considering other active sessions.
strings.t-87a76206c5fe: Gameplay and difficulty settings live in CoopData/mod-config.json; server settings in CoopData/DedicatedServer/server-config.json. Workshop layouts can also use DedicatedServer/server-data/mod-config.json. Confirm active paths at boot and stop only the intended server before editing. Keys include battleSize (default 1000; about 400 suggested), autoPauseEnabled, goldFoodInfluenceChangeInSettlements, enablePlayerExecutions and enableHeroExecutions. Difficulty birth/death options include birthAndDeath, clanMemberDeathChance and battleDeath; keep the separate Birth and Aging module disabled.
strings.t-5e7da2999efc: First verify Coop-only operation. Copy a compatible mod folder into engine/Modules; its folder name must match the mod Id. In the server UI reload, enable, set load order and Save Mods, then restart only that intended server. Every client needs matching mods, versions and order. Official Discord reports War Sails, Birth and Aging Options and Fast Mode are unsupported on dedicated servers. Do not alter Steam subscriptions automatically.
strings.t-b1c7438e2aec: Dedicated logs: CoopData/DedicatedServer/logs/coop-server-{date}-{time}.log. Client: bin/Win64_Shipping_Client/Coop_client.log; in-game host: Coop_server.log. Case matters on Linux. Crashes can be under the prefix’s drive_c/ProgramData/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/crashes or Documents/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/Coop Crash Reports. Keep the crash report (the Send action can remove it), redact secrets and use the official support-ticket channel. Do not repeatedly rejoin a stalled session.
strings.t-491c5310ef89: VPS / Docker / Wine — validated Wine 11.0 headless path
strings.t-15247ac76637: Headless dedicated-server SERVING was validated in this guide’s disposable tests with WineHQ Wine 11.0 (image docker.io/tianon/wine:11.0.0 / winehq-stable 11.0.0 on Debian trixie) plus Xvfb. Debian stock Wine 8.0 failed the same recipe (virtual_setup_exception stack overflow; no SERVING). Wine 9 and 10 were not tested here — treat 11.0 as the validated version, not a proven minimum across every Wine release. Do not use distro apt/yum “wine” metapackages that resolve to Wine 8 as an end-to-end recommendation. Preserve the Workshop layout (DedicatedServer alongside bin/, GUI/, SubModule.xml). Prefer host networking for UDP; keep stdin_open/tty for the console. GPU is not required for SERVING; a display server (Xvfb is enough; some setups need MIT-SHM disabled) is. Official Discord also mentions Ubuntu + Wine + winbind + Xvfb as community hosting notes.
strings.t-aa9a53d42feb: The bannerlordcoop-server-manager project and the Unofficial Bannerlord Co-op Pterodactyl egg are community tools, not official support. Review their source and compatibility before use. This guide does not install them.
strings.t-99516bca0a57: The official FAQ says Linux is supported but Steam Deck is not; Deck reports vary (https://github.com/Bannerlord-Coop-Team/BannerlordCoop/issues/2162). Hosting and playing together is estimated at 8 CPU cores and 16 GB RAM, with a dedicated server. A running game instance is not required for dedicated hosting. Linux host-and-play transfer stalls are tracked in issue #2095.

strings.t-5f2cc50c6909: Compare full Bannerlord build identifiers as well as Co-op releases. Even minor build differences can stall joining. Check the server log for the refused build or mod. Save cleanly, stop only the intended server, then back up CoopData and any distribution server-data before replacing files. Never automate Workshop unsubscribe/resubscribe or restart Steam during someone’s active session.
strings.t-021ca541456a: Windows exit -1073741819 indicates access violation; check blocked/missing DLLs and retained save backups. -532462766 indicates an unhandled .NET exception. Exit 1 is generic. These official FAQ diagnostics were not deliberately reproduced here.

rich.faq-versions-match:
Everyone must run the identical Co-op release and the exact Bannerlord build. A matching major version is not enough.

If joining fails, compare both builds first, then read the server's refusal log.
rich.faq-cant-connect:
Open the server's port on the host , and forward the same port on your router.

  • Direct connect needs both steps ().
  • can still block joins: ask your ISP for a public address, or use a private network.
  • Steam Join needs lobby mode and a logged-in Steam client; it does not fix every NAT issue.
rich.faq-platforms:
Each setup has one rule:

  • Steam Deck: use Desktop Mode (not officially supported).
  • Bazzite: check for Steam first; do not install a second copy.
  • Steam: the library and permissions live in the Flatpak sandbox.
  • hosts: prefer existing tools, Flatpak or a tool container over changing the base OS.
rich.faq-proton:
Use the Co-op release's recommended /GE build, or one already known to run Bannerlord. Find the real proton executable; paths vary.

  • Stock 8 failed headless serving here.
  • WineHQ Wine 11.0 + was validated.
  • Wine 9/10 and are untested here.

Do not break a working game install just to try the server.
rich.faq-server-crash:
Read the terminal output and the logs first.

  1. Check the exact game and Co-op builds.
  2. Check the extraction and runtime paths.
  3. For exit code 25, read starter_log.txt under ProgramData/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/logs.

Never delete saves as a shortcut.
rich.faq-workshop-updates:
Yes. The can update the client before the server, or lag behind because releases need TaleWorlds approval.

Compare the exact builds and restore a compatible pair. Restart Steam only when it is safe for active sessions; this guide does not change your subscriptions.
rich.faq-gpu-display:
No. A does not need a running Bannerlord game instance.

  • GPU- and display-free operation on every VPS is still unverified.
  • Steam lobby mode needs a logged-in Steam client; direct-IP mode is separate.
rich.faq-update-safely:
Back up first, then update.

  1. Save cleanly and stop only the intended server.
  2. Back up its entire CoopData directory and any separate server-data folder.
  3. Extract the update separately; keep your configuration and saves.
  4. Match the client and game builds, then verify startup.
rich.faq-keep-running:
After one successful manual start, wrap the same command in a user service.

Check logs with journalctl --user -u YOUR_UNIT. OpenRC and runit templates vary by distro and are unverified.

Never reuse a live production unit for a test.
rich.faq-logs-saves:
Under , open the selected prefix at this path:

drive_c/users/steamuser/Documents/Mount and Blade II Bannerlord/CoopData/DedicatedServer

  • Logs are in logs/.
  • Saves are in Game Saves/.

Confirm the paths printed at boot (--data-dir can change them) and back up before editing.
rich.faq-dedicated-download:
Use the release changelog and manifest. The Win64 .7z is on the Co-op CDN and may be missing from GitHub Assets.

The setup script checks its checksum. SteamCMD is not a substitute for this archive.
rich.faq-watchdog:
Official Discord reports say disabling it can help. Rename the client watchdog directory instead of deleting it, and keep a backup.

  • Caveat from the developers: crash logs are then unavailable for support.
  • --no-watchdog is server-only.
  • Do not change a running game.
rich.faq-workshop-ds:
Yes: the item includes DedicatedServer.

Steam keeps it on the latest approved release automatically, but TaleWorlds approval can lag behind GitHub/CDN. The host and every player must still match.

Do not enable manual Modules/Coop and Workshop Co-op together.
rich.faq-ports:
Allow 4200–4201 through the host, router and cloud , with steam:false. That is the official Discord recommendation.

Steam player-hosted invites can bypass , but dedicated-server Steam listing under / is unverified here.
rich.faq-no-udp-eula:
A new server often waits for an interactive answer before it opens the port.

  1. Read EULA.md and LICENSE.txt.
  2. Accept only if you agree.
  3. Start the service and confirm a SERVING log line.

Do not automate consent or copy another server's acceptance file.
rich.faq-linux-deck:
Linux is supported; Steam Deck is not. That is the official FAQ's position.

Deck reports vary; see issue #2162. This is a Linux setup guide.
rich.faq-host-and-play:
It can work, but expect trouble. The official FAQ suggests an 8-core CPU and 16 GB RAM.

Linux host-and-play can stall during character transfer (issue #2095). A separate may help; this guide does not promise a fix.
rich.faq-difficulty:
Difficulty and battle settings live in CoopData/mod-config.json. Server connection settings are in CoopData/DedicatedServer/server-config.json.

  • Stop the intended server before editing.
  • Lower battleSize for battle performance.
  • Back up before regenerating a config with missing options.
rich.faq-epic-steam:
No. Steam lobbies are Steam-to-Steam.

Epic and non-Steam installs need Direct IP with the configured port, or a suitable private network. Everyone still needs identical game and Co-op builds.
rich.faq-client-server-match:
They must match. The staging resolver downloads matching client and assets from one release.

Compare Modules/Coop/SubModule.xml with the server release tag in RESOLVED_VERSION.txt. The script warns when they differ.
rich.faq-ai-assistant:
Yes, but check what it tells you. An AI assistant can help explain this guide, but it may miss Bannerlord-specific details or suggest wrong fixes.

Check every command against the guide before you run it.

nav.dd_arch: A rolling-release, do-it-yourself distro with the newest packages and the AUR.
nav.dd_manjaro: An Arch-based rolling release with a friendlier installer and curated updates.
nav.dd_suse: Tumbleweed (rolling) and Leap (stable) from the SUSE community, with zypper and YaST.
nav.dd_bazzite: A gaming-ready immutable OS built on Fedora that updates as a single image (Silverblue-style systems fit here too).
nav.dd_deck: Valve's handheld and its SteamOS: a read-only system, so use Desktop Mode and keep changes small.
nav.dd_nix: A declarative, reproducible Linux that is configured entirely through Nix.
nav.dd_other: Gentoo, Void, Alpine or anything else: you get the generic commands to adapt.
